comparison: Both strongly support the generation of the comprehensive snRNAseq dataset (C3, C21, C108, C140). OpenEval emphasizes technical documentation and public availability; peer reviewers praise it as 'the first complete fracture repair atlas' and 'valuable publicly accessible dataset.' Full agreement on this contribution's value.

Significant disagreement on sample size adequacy. OpenEval finds the clustering and cell population identification well-supported (C28-C32, C110-C111). However, peer Reviewer 1 explicitly questions whether 1,189 nuclei (day 0) and 6,213 nuclei (combined) are sufficient, stating datasets may be 'underpowered to discern subtle biological changes.' OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer rates UNCERTAIN.

Partial overlap on cell population identification (C28-C32, C110). OpenEval provides detailed support for clustering methodology and marker validation. Peer reviewers accept the characterization without methodological concerns, noting the dataset will enable community reexamination of markers. Both supportive but focus on different aspects.

Both support the SSPC identification and functional validation (C34-C35). OpenEval notes CFU assays and grafting experiments with modest sample sizes. Peer reviewers accept 'convincing transcriptome analyses and experimental validation' for Pi16/Ly6a-expressing SSPCs. Agreement on experimental support despite OpenEval noting statistical limitations.

Perfect agreement on marker specificity findings (C36, C113-C114). Both recognize that commonly used markers are expressed across multiple clusters, challenging their specificity. OpenEval calls this 'an important negative result'; peer reviewers emphasize the dataset's value for 'reexamining expression of reported markers.' Full concordance.

Both support temporal dynamics of cell populations during healing (C37-C41, C115). OpenEval emphasizes integration methodology and quantified compositional changes. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'unique cell populations specific to fracture conditions' and temporal progression from fibroblasts to chondrocytes to osteoblasts. Strong agreement.

Critical disagreement on spatial organization interpretation (C42-C53). OpenEval finds spatial data well-supported by immunofluorescence and RNAscope. However, peer Reviewer 1 raises fundamental concern that 'POSTN is expressed in the cambium layer without fracture' and 'current data do not exclude the possibility that these pre-existing POSTN+ cells are the main responder' rather than arising from SSPCs. OpenEval SUPPORTED vs peer UNCERTAIN.

Strong agreement on IIFC identification and trajectory analysis (C54-C59, C118-C122, C124). Both accept pseudotime analysis showing SSPC→IIFC→differentiated cell trajectories. OpenEval notes this is computational inference requiring lineage tracing for causality. Peer reviewers accept this as a major finding with 'convincing transcriptome analyses and experimental validation.' Both SUPPORTED with similar caveats.

Both support grafting experiments validating differentiation trajectory (C60-C63). OpenEval notes modest sample sizes and population-level rather than single-cell tracking. Peer reviewers acknowledge grafting as supporting evidence, though concern about pre-existing POSTN+ cells (from R7) creates interpretive uncertainty. Agreement on data quality, some tension on interpretation.

Full agreement on IIFC characterization through GO analysis and gene expression (C64-C67). OpenEval finds comprehensive characterization with low apoptosis supporting differentiation over elimination. Peer reviewers accept these computational analyses as generating 'new hypotheses regarding periosteal cell reactions.' Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on GRN/SCENIC analysis and fibro-core identification (C68-C76, C94). OpenEval finds methodology sound with novel fibro-core discovery, noting regulon interpretation as one possibility. Peer reviewers explicitly praise 'cutting-edge algorithms including SCENIC' for defining cell roles. Both SUPPORTED with enthusiasm for computational approaches.

Full agreement on Notch signaling enrichment in IIFCs (C78-C80, C128). OpenEval notes clear pathway enrichment but lack of functional testing (correlative). Peer reviewers accept Notch as one of the key signaling pathways identified in gene cores. Both SUPPORTED with understanding that findings are computational/correlative.

Strong agreement on chondro-core identification and circadian clock involvement (C81-C88, C131-C132, C135). OpenEval finds temporal dynamics well-documented with novel circadian regulon discovery, noting inference rather than causal testing. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight 'circadian clock signaling' as major finding. Both SUPPORTED.

Full agreement on osteo-core and Wnt pathway involvement (C89-C93, C129-C130). OpenEval documents clear enrichment and temporal progression, noting lack of functional causation testing. Peer reviewers explicitly mention 'Wnt' and praise STRING network analysis. Both SUPPORTED with similar caveats about computational nature.

Strong agreement on CellChat analysis and cell-cell interactions (C95-C100, C136). OpenEval finds computational analysis methodologically appropriate but notes predictions don't prove functional interactions. Peer reviewers praise 'CellChat' among cutting-edge algorithms. Both SUPPORTED, recognizing computational prediction limitations.

Strong agreement on ligand-receptor analysis and IIFC paracrine role (C101-C107, C137-C139). OpenEval finds temporal dynamics well-documented but functional consequences inferred rather than tested. Peer reviewers accept that 'IIFCs are the main source of paracrine signals' suggesting 'crucial paracrine role.' Both SUPPORTED with understanding of computational prediction nature.

OpenEval evaluates background/rationale claims (C1-C2, C9-C20) as SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—peer reviews focus on novel findings rather than background claims.
OpenEval finds C27 (snRNAseq advantages) SUPPORTED by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation—methodological justification not explicitly addressed by reviewers.
OpenEval finds C116-C117 (prior knowledge gaps) SUPPORTED, providing study motivation. No corresponding peer review evaluation—reviewers don't explicitly assess background knowledge claims.
OpenEval finds C123 (fibrogenic response parallel to muscle repair) SUPPORTED by citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this contextual claim.

OpenEval finds C125-C127 (prior Notch literature) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation—reviewers accept Notch findings without separately evaluating background claims.
OpenEval finds C133-C134 (Bmal1 in cartilage literature) SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims.

Partial overlap on major integrated conclusions. OpenEval evaluates C4-C8, C23-C26, C94, C141-C142 as SUPPORTED by convergent evidence, noting some aspects remain correlative. Peer reviewers focus on subset (C5, C24, C54-C59, C118-C122, C124) accepting IIFC as 'characteristic cell type' and 'progenitor undergoing osteochondrogenic differentiation.' Agreement on core IIFC concept.

OpenEval rates C143 (therapeutic potential) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's speculative about future applications without testing whether manipulating IIFCs enhances healing. No corresponding peer review evaluation—reviewers don't assess forward-looking therapeutic claims.
